question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}2p+4q=-6 \\ \frac{3p}{2}+\frac{5q}{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$p=$
{{field-1}}$,\,q=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $2.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2p+4q=-6 \\ \frac{3p}{2}+\frac{5q}{2}=2 & |\,\times 2\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2p+4q=-6 \\ 3p+5q=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $p$ in the first equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2p+4q & =-6 \\ 2p & =-4q-6 \\ p & =-2q-3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can substitute $p=-2q-3$ into the second equation and solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3p+5q & =4 \\ 3(-2q-3)+5q & =4 \\ -6q-9+5q & =4 \\ -q & =13 \\ q & =-13\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, to find the value of $p,$ we substitute $q=-13$ into the equation $p=-2q-3,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =-2q-3 \\  & =-2(-13)-3 \\  & =26-3 \\  & =23\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=23,\,q=-13.$
